contentObjective: I can make and read a box plot to summarize a data set.
languageObjective: I can explain my box plot using the words box plot, median, quartile, and interquartile range.

vocabulary.termEs: Representar datos con diagramas de caja
vocabulary.definition: Show a data set's five-number summary in a box-and-whisker display.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mostrar el resumen de cinco números de un conjunto de datos en un diagrama de caja y bigotes.
vocabulary.cloze: A box plot shows the ___-number summary: least, Q1, median, Q3, greatest.

examples.text: A box from Q1 75.5 to Q3 88 with whiskers to 68 and 94
examples.why: All five summary numbers are placed.

examples.text: A bar chart of the same scores

vocabulary.definition: A graph that shows how data is spread using five key numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una gráfica que muestra cómo se reparten los datos con cinco números clave.
vocabulary.visual: A box from Q1 to Q3 with a line at the median, and whiskers from min to max
vocabulary.cloze: A graph that shows data with a box and whiskers based on the five-number summary is a ___.

examples.text: A box holding the middle half, with whiskers to the extremes
A line graph of scores over time

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.
vocabulary.cloze: The middle value of the data, shown as a line inside the box, is the ___.

examples.why: The middle value once the numbers are in order.
Middle of an unsorted list is not the median.

vocabulary.definition: Numbers that split the data into four equal parts.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números que dividen los datos en cuatro partes iguales.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 → Q1 = 4 (median of lower half), Q3 = 12 (median of upper half)
vocabulary.cloze: A value that divides the data into four equal parts is a ___.

examples.why: It is the median OF that half.
That is the minimum, not a quartile.

vocabulary.definition: The spread of the middle half of the data (Q3 − Q1).
vocabulary.definitionEs: La extensión de la mitad central de los datos (Q3 − Q1).
vocabulary.visual: If Q1 = 12 and Q3 = 20, then IQR = 20 − 12 = 8 — the middle 50% spans 8 units
vocabulary.cloze: The distance between the first and third quartiles, showing the middle 50% of data, is the ___.

examples.why: Q3 minus Q1 — the middle half's width.
That is the range, using the extremes.

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.visual: A box plot where the median is centered in the box shows symmetric distribution
vocabulary.cloze: The way data values are spread out is the ___.

examples.text: “Most scores cluster near 85, with one down at 68”
examples.why: It says where the data sits and how it spreads.
One value describes a point, not the shape of the set.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.visual: Small IQR = low variability in the middle 50%. Large IQR = high variability
vocabulary.cloze: How spread out the data values are is the ___.

examples.why: The values differ, which is what variability measures.
Nothing varies, so there is no spread to describe.

items.meaning: Show a data set's five-number summary in a box-and-whisker display
The middle number when you put them in order

steps: 1. 5-Number Summary: Minimum, Lower Quartile (Q1), Median (Q2), Upper Quartile (Q3), Maximum
2. Draw the Box: The box spans from Q1 to Q3 and contains the middle 50% of data
3. Whiskers: Draw lines from the box out to the minimum and maximum

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Average Monthly Temperatures
revealWordProblem.text: The box plots show the average monthly temperatures for the same month in Chicago, IL, and Honolulu, HI. How do the monthly temperatures between the two cities compare?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two box plots of average monthly temperatures in degrees Fahrenheit, one for Honolulu, Hawaii and one for Chicago, Illinois.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Chicago's five-number summary is about Min = 26°F, Q1 = 34°F, Median = 57°F, Q3 = 74°F, Max = 90°F, giving a range of 90 − 26 = 64°F and an IQR of 74 − 34 = 40°F. Honolulu's five-number summary is about Min = 78°F, Q1 = 82°F, Median = 84°F, Q3 = 86°F, Max = 89°F, giving a range of 89 − 78 = 11°F and an IQR of 86 − 82 = 4°F. Honolulu's median (84°F) is 84 − 57 = 27°F warmer than Chicago's (57°F), and Honolulu's temperatures are far more consistent (range 11°F, IQR 4°F) than Chicago's, which swing widely across the year (range 64°F, IQR 40°F) — showing Chicago has hot summers and cold winters while Honolulu stays warm and steady year-round.

reviewCheck.stem: Two box plots show: Team A has IQR = 8, Team B has IQR = 22. What does this tell you?
choices: Team A's middle 50% is more consistent; Team B's is more spread out
Team B is a better team
Team A has a higher median
The IQRs don't tell you about consistency
reviewCheck.explanation: A smaller IQR means the middle 50% of data is more tightly clustered. Team A's scoring is more consistent in the middle range.
choiceFeedback: Bigger IQR doesn't mean better—it means more variation.
IQR is always about consistency in the middle 50%.
hints: IQR measures the width of the box — how spread out the MIDDLE 50% of each team's scores is.
Compare a narrow box (IQR 8) with a wide box (IQR 22). Ask what narrow vs wide says about consistency — not about which team is better.
First step: translate each number — Team A's middle scores span only 8 points; Team B's span 22. Then choose the statement that matches.
reviewCheck.stemEs: Dos diagramas de caja muestran: el equipo A tiene un RIC = 8 y el equipo B tiene un RIC = 22. ¿Qué te dice esto?
reviewCheck.explanationEs: Un RIC más pequeño significa que el 50% central de los datos está más agrupado. La anotación del equipo A es más consistente en el rango central.
choicesEs: El 50% central del equipo A es más consistente; el del equipo B está más disperso
El equipo B es mejor equipo
El equipo A tiene una mediana más alta
Los RIC no dicen nada sobre la consistencia
hintsEs: El RIC mide el ancho de la caja: qué tan dispersos están los puntajes del 50% CENTRAL de cada equipo.
Compara una caja angosta (RIC 8) con una caja ancha (RIC 22). Pregunta qué dice angosta frente a ancha sobre la consistencia, no sobre qué equipo es mejor.
Primer paso: traduce cada número — los puntajes centrales del Equipo A abarcan solo 8 puntos; los del Equipo B abarcan 22. Luego elige el enunciado que coincida.
